BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.
BYD October EV sales reach a record 300,000+
The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.
BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.
To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.
BYD October 2026 NEV sales (Source: BYD)
BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.
According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.
BYD “Xi’an” car carrier loading Dolphin Surf EVs for Europe (Source: BYD)
Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.
By the end of 2026, BYD expects overseas shipments to reach about 2 million vehicles. In 2027, that number is expected to rise to more than 2.5 million vehicles.
BYD opens first Flash Chargers in Germany (Source: Klaus Hartmann/ BYD)
With several new and updated vehicles launching with its new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, BYD aims to continue attracting new buyers with longer range, faster charging, and more tech-oriented models.
Electrek’s Take
While the US is coming off its best quarter of the year in EV sales, BYD’s performance shows how far ahead China is in the transition to electric vehicles.
China continues to lead the global EV market, accounting for over half of all electric cars sold worldwide.
With a wave of low-cost domestic brands flooding China’s market, BYD and other automakers are driving growth overseas in major markets like Europe, South Korea, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America, where legacy OEMs are already falling behind quickly.

PARIS — Swedish defense manufacturer Saab has unveiled the Combat Boat 90 (CB90) CX, a drone boat designed to strike targets beyond the horizon and counter short-range aerial threats, to equip the Swedish Navy.
The company introduced the new speed assault boat Sunday morning before the Euronaval defense show taking pl ace in Paris this week. The CB90CX is designed to operate entirely without a human crew on board, according to Saab, and is promoted as a larger, heavier payload platform than the existing 16.3m-long CB90 Next-Generation (CB90 NG), which is already in service with nine navies globally.
“One of the key distinctions is that the CB90 NG can be upgraded for optionally crewed operations, whereas the CB90CX is designed for uncrewed operations from the outset,” Anders Hellman, head of Saab’s business unit Docksta, told Breaking Defense today.
The CB90CX is 18m long, and according to Hellman, its larger hull increases payload capacity by over 50 percent. He added that it is also integrated with an entirely new vessel infrastructure, which includes an integrated ship automation and monitoring system, fire control system, and steer-by-wire technology.
The new CB90 CX is envisioned to be available in three configurations: an intelligence and surveillance variant relying on Saab’s Giraffe 1X radar; an anti-ship warfare role to enable beyond-line-of-sight strikes against surface vessels; and a short-range air defense variant. The air defense variant will be made possible by equipping the boat with an anti-aircraft automatic cannon that could down uncrewed threats such as drones, according to the manufacturer.
“The capabilities offered through our proposed configurations are well-aligned with the broader operational requirements and future direction outlined in the Swedish Armed Forces Amphibious Battalion 2030 concept,” Hellman said.
The Amphibious Battalion 2030 concept is a modernization program that seeks to shift the Scandinavian country’s traditional coastal defense strategy toward a more mobile, dispersed maritime force. In practice, this means that rather than adopting larger platforms, naval units will use smaller, fast platforms intended to be scattered across the islands and shallow waters of the Baltic Sea and Nordic archipelagos.
The craft is already under production, destined for the Swedish Navy as the launch customer. Hellman could not disclose delivery timelines, only that these will “co-exist” with the service’s existing CB90 NG boats.
In Q2 of 2025, the Swedish Defence Material Administration, or FMV, placed an order for 22 CB90NGs, valued at about 900 million SEK ($92 million) . It was intended to replace some of the 16 CB90s the country has provided to the Ukrainian Armed Forces, as part of previous support packages.

Qualcomm this morning is announcing that it has completed the initial validation of its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) memory architecture, which will be a central part of the company’s upcoming Dragonfly data center AI accelerators. The stacked memory architecture will see Qualcomm and its manufacturing partners place multiple layers of DRAM on top of a small compute die in order to bring memory even closer to the compute hardware that is accessing it, allowing Qualcomm to reap the energy efficiency and cost efficiency benefits of a closer hardware placement.
The recent validation of the technology moves HBC one step closer to deployment in commercial products, which are scheduled to start sampling next year. Qualcomm has now validated that the technology works and is delivering energy efficiency and memory bandwidth close to their expectations, allowing them to move towards mass production next year while keeping customers (and investors) in the loop on the development of Qualcomm’s Dragonfly AI250 accelerator and its successors.
Qualcomm HBC: Near Memory Compute for Less Data Movement
First announced by Qualcomm back at their 2026 Investor Day , HBC is a new Qualcomm-spearheaded technology that is intending to use near-memory compute in order to strike a new balance between memory capacity, memory performance, and production costs – with Qualcomm looking to push the envelope on all three aspects.
Fundamentally, the technology is a further variation on HBM and other memory stacking technologies. But unlike HBM where multiple DRAM dies are stacked on top of a base die that is connected back to the host processor over an ultra-wide memory bus, HBC aims to cut out the middleman by placing a small compute die at the bottom of the stack instead.
Qualcomm HBC Accelerator Diagram Solid
In principle, placing memory on top of a compute die has several benefits. The biggest of these is energy efficiency, as moving data around costs energy – and moving large amounts of data large distances costs even more energy. By placing memory on top of a compute die, this eliminates even the relatively short distance of an HBM connection (to say nothing of external memory like LPDDR5X), minimizing the amount of energy spent to move that data around. Those energy savings, in turn, can be funneled back into improving performance of the chip itself, or allowing a larger number of chips to be clustered together within the same energy footprint.
The compute die itself is not a full processor. But by placing the most memory bandwidth-intensive operations on the die and then sending the results from that back to the larger compute die at the center of the processor, Qualcomm is looking to get their memory and compute hardware as close together as is feasible.
Qualcomm HBC Compared to HBM Solid
Qualcomm’s efforts are also eyeing production costs here. Because of the wide memory bus used by HBM, it required advanced packaging such as CoWoS or EMIB to connect HBM stacks to a compute die and memory controllers. But by shifting most of the computational workload to the compute die that sits under the memory, far less memory bandwidth is needed to connect the compute die to a larger processor die elsewhere on the chip package. And, consequently, that connection can be built with cheaper technologies such as traditional 2D organic substrates.
Qualcomm HBC vs HBM Detailed
That said, HBC does not eliminate all of the complexity. Like HBM, it still requires bonding multiple DRAM dies (or in Qualcomm’s case: wafers) on top of another die using TSVs, which is itself a challenging process. Which means the need for complex manufacturing techniques has not gone away, but it has been reduced from both memory stacking and die-to-die connectivity to just the memory stacking.
Finally, Qualcomm is looking to strike a better balance between memory bandwidth and memory capacity here. Notably, the company’s HBC design calls for using LPDDR5X DRAM dies here rather than the thin, high-performance dies used by HBM. The company has not outlined what the final performance of the technology will be, but the capacity of an HBC stack is already projected to be larger than what current HBM4 implementations can achieve.
Qualcomm HBC vs HBM vs SRAM
Qualcomm’s fundamental argument through all of this is that HBC provides a better all-around solution than any other memory architecture, be it HBM, on-die SRAM, or off-package LPDDR. As proposed, HBC has strengths and weaknesses versus all of these technologies, but as Qualcomm argues, they can achieve memory bandwidth (and thus performance) far better than external LPDDR – and approaching HBM – without the capacity constraints of using on-die SRAM, or the high costs of the latter of those two solutions.
Ultimately, all of this is meant to lead to allowing Qualcomm to build a better chip for AI inference, by meeting inference’s need for memory bandwidth and capacity with fewer drawbacks than existing technologies. It
Validating HBC: 2 Stack Test Finds 5x Bandwidth-per-Watt of HBM4
Diving into the validation process itself, for their initial HBC validation Qualcomm has hooked up an early HBC sample stack to a test unit in their San Diego labs.
Qualcomm HBC ATE Test Rig
While the test setup itself is not much to look at, inside of it is a chip that, for Qualcomm, is critical to their data center plans.
Given that this was an early sample, it should be noted that HBC stack they were working with here just had 2 layers of DRAM dies. Shipping products will have 4 layers. So Qualcomm is not yet at the point where they are testing full-sized stacks.
Qualcomm HBC Validaiton How We Measure It
Briefly outlining their validation approach, Qualcomm tells us that they used the HBC test stack with an automated tester, which was used to measure the stack as both an LPDDR5X device and as an HBC device.
Qualcomm HBC Validation Findings
Ultimately, Qualcomm had three major findings with their successful validation testing. The first, of course, being that this worked at all, proving that it can be done. Meanwhile in regards to performance, Qualcomm measured their HBC solution as delivering more than five-times the energy efficiency (on a bandwidth-per-watt basis) than HBM4 as per its own specifications. Finally, while the company is not disclosing specific bandwidth figures, they are categorizing the measured bandwidth at 18x higher than external LPDDR5X.
The energy efficiency figure in particular is a bit short of Qualcomm’s initial projections for the technology, where they were hoping to beat HBM4 by 6x. But if this carries over to a full product, it still represents a significant improvement in efficiency.
According to Qualcomm, their validation testing also includes the thermal behaviors of the product, though the company has not gone into any further detail there. Qualcomm has had little to say on the subject so far, but thermal considerations are one of the major technical hurdles they will need to overcome, as a more active compute die as the base die in a stacked memory architecture is expected to put out more heat.
Final Words
With their initial HBC validation complete, Qualcomm is now looking at moving on to the next step of commercialization of the technology with their Dragonfly AI250 accelerator. The successor to the Dragonfly AI200 accelerator due this year, AI250 will be the first product to integrate HBC – and it will be a key part of future Qualcomm AI accelerators after that. AI250 does not have a launch date yet, but according to Qualcomm it will begin sampling in H1 of this year, which is potentially a move-up for the company’s plans following the initial announcement that sampling would take place earlier this year.
If everything pans out with HBC, the technology will not be limited to Dragonfly AI accelerators, either. Qualcomm has previously announced that they would also be bringing the technology to their consumer-focused Snapdragon products – though the company is not specifying when and what products at the time.
Qualcomm HBC Summary
Ultimately, HBC is a play for energy efficiency and a lower TCO for Qualcomm. If the technology pans out, the company expects to be able to deliver AI inference accelerators that are both more energy efficient and cheaper to build than contemporary designs. Which in turn would make them cheaper to operate (and ideally, cheaper to acquire) than GPUs for large AI inference operations. We will get to see how that plays out over the coming months as Qualcomm moves towards sampling Dragonfly AI250 in the first half of next year.

Oshkosh Defense announced Monday a partnership with Silicon Valley startup Grid Aero to manufacture large military drones, which would be the first aircraft produced by the Wisconsin-based company.
“We do things that like gravity and stay on the ground,” said Logan Jones, Oshkosh’s chief growth officer, in an interview with Defense News, describing the company’s typical offerings. But he called the partnership “a very nice fit for us.”
Jones said the partnership grew out of the Defense Department’s Arsenal of Freedom campaign, which aims to expand the domestic industrial base. Grid Aero needed a partner to help scale production, while Oshkosh was looking to manufacture something with long-term potential.
“We looked where both the market was growing, and where the technology class would benefit from scale,” he said, explaining why the company has been exploring unmanned systems . Oshkosh was drawn to Grid Aero in part because its Lifter aircraft uses metal construction rather than composite materials, aligning with Oshkosh’s manufacturing capabilities.
Although Oshkosh would technically be considered a subcontractor, Jones said the companies describe the arrangement as a partnership because Oshkosh is helping Grid Aero reconfigure the Lifter aircraft “to ensure that manufacturability is at the heart of their design and strategy from day one, not an afterthought.”
However, Oshkosh wasn’t the only company making a decision. For Grid Aero, Oshkosh’s extensive experience in defense manufacturing helped solidify the decision to work together, co-founder and CEO Arthur Dubois said.
“They build vehicles by the thousands, and that is the rate we need. Their lines are also built for variety. A single Oshkosh line can build many variants of a vehicle, each set up for a different mission, without slowing down. Lifter works the same way,” Dubois said in an email to Defense News.
Founded in 2024, Grid Aero developed the Lifter, an autonomous aircraft with modular payload capacity that the company describes as a “pickup truck of the skies.” The Lifter falls into the Group 4 or Group 5 category of unmanned aerial systems, classifications that cover aircraft weighing more than 1,320 pounds.
Dubois said Oshkosh’s manufacturing technology is a good fit for the Lifter because it is “simple, rugged, piston-powered, and made from ubiquitous materials.” He added that the Lifter’s design “borrows as much from military trucks as from traditional aircraft.”
The companies plan to build thousands of Lifter aircraft for the Defense Department and commercial customers. Initially, Grid Aero will conduct low-rate production while Oshkosh establishes a pilot production line.
“As customer demand grows, we will move production to Oshkosh in stages and keep pace with what the customer needs,” Jones said. “As [the Defense Department] plans for future conflicts, the ability to field and replace aircraft at scale is one of the most important advantages it can build.”

The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid Is Now on Sale in the US, but Only in SR Technology Package Flavor
16 photos
Photo: Nissan
Finally available to configure in the US market, Nissan's heavily anticipated Rogue Hybrid is heavily restricted at launch. While its build & price tool may read $35,490 for the base SV grade, prospective customers are presented with a pricier trim level for the time being.
SR with the SR Technology Package is how said configuration is called, and the $41,490 starting price does not include $1,575 for destination and delivery. Both the SV and the range-topping Platinum don't reach showrooms until January 2027. Even so, the sole trim level available right now loads the compact-sized crossover with a lot of desirable stuff.
I find the single-trim launch approach rather interesting because most automakers either launch the best- or least-equipped model first. Nissan , by comparison, put a feature-rich version of the Rogue Hybrid in front of the first wave of customers. The SR Technology Package adds $4,000 to the SR's advertised price, with that money getting you better tech and more convenience.
To understand what you're getting, let's first run through some SR highlights: quilted TailorFit seating, 19-inch alloys, dual 12.3-inch screens for instrumentation and infotainment, Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto. Both wireless, of course! Opting for the SR Technology Package upgrades the tech side of the cabin to 14.3 inches for both screens.
Google built-in goodies, a memory driver's seat, memory outside mirrors, a power liftgate, panoramic roof, plus advanced ProPILOT Assist functionality also need mentioning. Said package further includes 3D HD Enhanced Intelligent Around View Monitor with Invisible Hood View and Front Wide View, a heated steering wheel, rear automatic braking, front and rear parking sensors, and gloss-black roof rails. In other words, $4,000 does get you a lot of things.
Photo: Nissan Every grade ships with standard all-wheel drive, and every grade of the Rogue Hybrid relies on a 1.5-liter turbo inline-three without the VC-Turbo nonsense of the combustion-only Rogue. Gifted with a fixed 13.0:1 compression ratio, this mill is used exclusively for generating electricity, making the Rogue Hybrid stand out from conventional hybrid crossovers.
Said engine is tuned for a narrow operating window that prioritizes efficiency over power. Its thermal efficiency is very high, with Nissan claiming a 42% thermal efficiency. Going forward, Nissan hopes to achieve 50% in the coming years through advancements in ultra-lean burn combustion, strict fixed-point operation, and comprehensive waste heat recovery.
Good for up to 225 horsepower in optimal conditions, the Rogue Hybrid uses two electric motors and a 1.67-kWh battery pack. There is no charging plug to speak of, as that would defeat the purpose of a hybrid. Optimized for its charge and discharge ability, said battery works together with the internal combustion engine to keep those electric drive units spinning.
Advertised with the quietest and quickest acceleration in the class, the Rogue Hybrid also promises best-in-class braking from 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) to zero. As far as fuel economy is concerned, the EPA-estimated figures are 41 miles per gallon in the city and 36 on the highway.
That's 38 mpg (6.2 l/100 km) combined versus a best of 31 (7.6) for the internal combustion Rogue with all-wheel drive or 32 (7.4) with front-wheel drive. Unfortunately, the combined 38-mpg estimate isn't good enough by Toyota standards. The EPA lists 42 mpg (5.6 l/100 km) for the RAV4 Hybrid with all-wheel drive, and that rival is the single best-selling hybrid crossover in the US as of this writing.

Toyota’s luxury brand Lexus is launching a new electric SUV in 2027, its first vehicle built in China in over two decades.
Lexus leans on China for next-gen EV in 2027
It’s official. Toyota is breaking from tradition, planning to develop and produce the new vehicle in China rather than its home market of Japan.
Lexus confirmed the new vehicle will be made at its new manufacturing plant in Jinshan, Shanghai, and will go on sale in 2027.
As the first Lexus factory built from scratch overseas, the company said the new plant will bring together its global manufacturing capabilities.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Toyota broke ground on the facility in June 2025, saying the new facility will unlock “Lexus speed” as it aims to keep pace with domestic brands like BYD. Construction was expected to be completed this past August, with the first vehicle scheduled to roll off the assembly line in the fall of 2027.
The first Lexus model will be an electric SUV, produced using advanced manufacturing methods such as gigacasting to reduce costs and speed up output.
The facility will be a cornerstone of Toyota’s comeback plans in China, where it’s struggled to compete with local brands.
Production capacity will be around 1,000 units per month in 2027 as Toyota ramps up to “tens of thousands” in 2028.
Toyota’s sales plunged nearly 20% in China last month, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower sales than the year prior. The market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected,” Toyota said.
Lexus TZ (left) and ES (right) Source: Lexus China
In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, 18.9% fewer than in the same period last year.
Lexus’ new Shanghai facility is wholly owned by Toyota, enabling it to produce vehicles in China through its joint ventures.
The new electric SUV will go on sale in China in 2027. Specific details, including battery, range, and prices, have yet to be announced.
Lexus TZ (Source: Lexus China)
As part of its “with China, for China, strategy, Lexus said it will “continue to use China as a source of innovation,” adding it will “deepen localization efforts” to bring classic models to the market that meet local needs.
Toyota joins the growing list of major OEMs that are already tapping, or plan to tap, China for its next-generation electric vehicles.
Electrek’s Take
While in other global markets, Toyota is sticking to its “multi-pathway” strategy, which includes all powertrains from electric to ICE; in China, it’s being forced to adapt.
China is Toyota’s third-largest market, following the US and Japan. To stay competitive and turn things around in China, Toyota will rely more on local partners and suppliers.
Developing the new Lexus electric SUV in China first rather than Japan is significant given Toyota’s traditional ways.
Typically, it takes Toyota about four to five years to fully develop a new vehicle. In China, automakers are now building them in as little as two years.
Toyota, like many automakers at this point, is turning to China for new tech, batteries, production methods, and other EV components to keep pace.

source_document.body:
KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is fitting drones with larger jam-resistant antennas , making it harder for Ukrainian forces to use electronic countermeasures to scramble their navigation signals, Ukrainian officials said.
Russia’s Kometa navigation modules, produced by the company VNIIR-Progress, use arrays of small receiving elements called patch antennas to keep satellite navigation working through jamming. They have been found on Geran drones, glide-bomb kits, Iskander-M and Kinzhal missiles and the new Filin cruise missile, according to a database of Russian weapons run by Ukraine’s military intelligence agency , HUR.
The Kremlin is already using Kometa modules with 16-element antenna arrays at scale and is setting up serial production of 20-element arrays, increasing its capability to work out which direction jamming comes from and compensate for it, HUR said Oct. 19.
Shaheds carrying antennas with 32 elements have already been found attacking Kyiv, said Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, an electronic-warfare specialist and adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on defense technology.
“The more elements, the more electronic-warfare signal sources the antenna can suppress,” he said in an October post on Telegram.
The larger antennas give Russia an asymmetric advantage by being easier to counter than to install, Beskrestnov said.
“This race is difficult for us because it is easier for the enemy to increase the number of elements on an antenna than it is for us to add electronic warfare sites,” Beskrestnov said.
Russia’s better-protected drones can fly through Ukraine’s EW shield — one of its most affordable and widespread layers of air defense — leaving more of them to be shot down by costlier options, like interceptor drones, jets and missiles .
A Kometa module’s resistance to jamming depends on the number and arrangement of its patch antennas, the receiving elements on the array, and on the algorithm its processing chip uses to separate the satellite signal from interference, HUR said.
Drones carrying the upgraded antennas can still be taken out by jamming more satellite bands at once or by networking devices to feed drones false coordinates, defense leaders say.
The commander of Ukraine’s Night Watch unit, who goes by the call sign Alkhimik, bought a 32-element antenna taken from a Shahed, “that had crashed and was being sold on the secondary market,” he told Militarnyi in July.
He discovered that the device was simply two 16-element arrays covering different satellite-navigation bands put together, he said, giving him inspiration on how to counter it.
“By creating two systems — one operating in the L1 band and the other covering L2/L5 — we’ll be able to jam this antenna without any problems,” Alkhimik said.
Spoofing works, too, according to Fly Group Ukraine. It links multiple devices into a network to feed a drone false coordinates, Anatoliy Khrapchynskyi, the defense company’s director of development, told Reuters in September.
“The drone continues to think it is flying toward its target, but its own autopilot, relying on the false coordinates, gradually changes course on its own and steers the craft away from cities into safe areas,” he said.
Russian defense firms have ordered more than 100,000 Kometa modules in various configurations this year to guide cruise and ballistic missiles, strike drones and guided bombs, HUR said, a measure of demand for the technology.

One in four supply chain leaders wish they had made a different warehouse automation decision, according to a new Exotec report. But changing course could be costly, as 94% say switching providers would be prohibitively expensive.
What’s Related
“Avoid Robot Regret” surveyed 250 supply chain decision-makers in the U.S. and Canada . The warehouse robotics company found that disappointment often starts with decisions made before a system is installed, including how buyers calculate costs and assign responsibility when something goes wrong.
“What we heard from supply chain leaders is that regret is rarely about the technology itself,” said Romain Moulin, CEO and co-founder of Exotec. “It starts when a system built by several vendors stops working as one, and the customer is left figuring out who is responsible for the fix. The operations that get the most from their automation are the ones where a single partner owns the whole system performance, from design through the years it runs.”
Larger companies also reported problems with their automation investments. Among respondents at companies with more than $1 billion in revenue, 21% said their biggest automation investment fell short of expectations, compared with 13% at smaller companies.
RELATED STORIES: The Skills Warehouse Companies Are Paying For Right Now | Robots for the Rest of Us: Warehouse Automation Gets Easier
Automation costs higher than expected
Nearly two-thirds of respondents, or 65%, said their total ownership costs were higher than expected. Yet 69% admitted they did not calculate the full lifetime cost before investing.
The report points to expenses that can be missing from an initial proposal, such as software and hardware upgrades or spare parts. Seven in 10 respondents said undisclosed automation costs had increased their annual maintenance expenses.
Overruns were biggest among buyers whose systems fell short of expectations. Within that group, 43% said total costs were 26% to 100% higher than anticipated.
Who fixes the system?
Most respondents (60%) had automation designed by multiple companies. One in seven leaders said they had not seen the benefits of automation because no vendor took full responsibility for system performance.
The report urges buyers to establish who will handle problems before signing a contract. It also recommends asking what maintenance includes and how support will continue if the project manager leaves.
Preparation was another trouble spot. More than a quarter of respondents, or 27%, said their warehouse wasn’t ready when they invested in automation.
Method Research prepared the online survey and RepData distributed it, with responses collected Aug. 17–31, 2026. Nearly every respondent, 249 of 250, had participated in an automation deployment at a current or previous employer.

Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.
The Toyota Corolla Cross is going electric
The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.
Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.
The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.
It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.
Toyota CEO Koji Sato reveals the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show (Source: Toyota)
“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.
Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.
New images from Chinese media outlet Autohome show what’s expected to be the all-electric Corolla Cross, with a closed-off grille and a unique body design.
The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s new “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrains.
Toyota hasn’t revealed specifics, including battery or powertrain specs, but the next-gen Corolla EV is expected to remain close in style to the Concept. Aside from the massive COROLLA badge on the back, it looks like an entirely different vehicle with a near sports-car-like silhouette.
In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company “cannot survive” if it does not adapt amid new competition and technology from China.
During the special, which went behind the scenes at Toyota’s “top secret” development site, several blurred Corolla Concept body types , including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were revealed in the background.
According to a recent Nikkei report, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.
Toyota CEO Koji Sato reveals the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show (Source: Toyota)
The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.
The hybrid version will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.
Toyota has yet to confirm the electric version will launch in the US. According to Car and Driver , the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.
Source: Autohome

Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys Almost-New Chevrolet Corvette Z06 for $25,000 Below MSRP

Every which way you spin it, this transaction looks like a steal. Even when you factor in the buyer's fee. Technically, the auction did close at roughly $25,000 under MSRP, but in reality, the buyer still had to pay a fee to the auction site. Regardless, it's an almost-new Z06 at a significant discount, and I don't know anyone who'd pass up such a deal.
I don't even mind the spec. Sure, it doesn't have additional carbon fiber elements or the Z07 package, and it's not a 3LZ variant, but you still get the bare minimum, and then some (like the optional front-axle lift system and GT2 bucket seats). These types of deals are very sought-after in the industry. It's not about lowballing the seller, as much as simply getting the most bang for your buck, which I believe is what happened here.
Could this Z06 have sold for even less? I guess it's possible, but not by much. Maybe another couple of grand at the absolute most. Keep in mind that it's barely been driven.
The Torch Red exterior is one controversial aspect to contend with, but that's such an easy fix - you just get it wrapped in whatever color you want and problem fixed! If you can afford a car for $110k+ (which is what this cost, buyer's fee included), you can certainly afford a $5k+ wrap from a quality shop. Then again, maybe you like the bright red exterior and you just leave it as-is.
Aside from its vibrant colorway, this Z06 Coupe also comes with Carbon Flash accents, a rear spoiler, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, plus a set of optional black-finished 20" front and 21" rear forged wheels wearing Michelin rubber and Brembo discs with red-finished calipers. I already mentioned the front-axle lift system, which comes with memory settings. It's a must-have as far as I'm concerned.

U.S. manufacturing activity remained in growth mode for a 10th straight month in October, with most key demand indicators remaining positive. The Monday update supported mostly positive demand commentary provided by public less-than-truckload carriers last week.
Manufacturing supply executives surveyed during the month returned a 55.5 reading for the Institute for Supply Management’s Manufacturing PMI. The report came in one percentage point ahead of analysts’ expectations and the September result . (A reading above 50 for the index signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction.)
A sustained level above 47.5 signals that the overall economy is growing. The October reading was consistent with annualized real GDP growth of 2.7%, which was up from a 2.4% level in September, the report said.
The new orders index—an indicator of future activity—also expanded for a 10th straight month, logging a 55.5 reading, 20 basis points higher than September. Four of the six largest manufacturing industries tracked—machinery; computer and electronics; transportation equipment; and chemical products—reported increases.
Demand sentiment around news orders improved to a 1.8-to-1 positive-to-negative ratio in the month compared to 1.7-to-1 in September.
The backlog of orders (54.6) dipped 1.8 points, but production (59) expanded to the highest level in five years, up 2.3 points sequentially.
Customers’ inventories (41.6) remained “too low,” with no sequential change in the reading. “A ‘too low’ status for the Customers’ Inventories Index is usually considered positive for future production,” the report said.
Manufacturing employment (52.4) remained in growth territory for a fourth straight month.
The supplier deliveries index (59.1), which measures delivery times to manufacturing facilities, has signaled slowing delivery times and supply chain constraints for 11 consecutive months. The dataset was 10 bps higher sequentially. (This ISM subindex is the only one that is inverted.)
Cost inflation remains a primary concern. The prices index (75.2) remained elevated, but 2.7 points below September.
Overall sentiment from respondents was classified as 34% positive and 66% negative, 800 bps worse than two months ago .
“Among negative comments, pricing volatility was mentioned in 62 percent, longer lead times 41 percent, tariffs 25 percent and the Iran war 21 percent; most comments mentioned multiple factors,” the report said.
Institute for Supply Management data typically leads changes in LTL shipments by approximately three months. Public LTL carrier tonnage flipped positive in March on a cumulative, year-over-year comparison. Carriers reported modestly improving demand trends last week in conjunction with third-quarter reports.
XPO ( NYSE: XPO ) said half of its customers expect stronger demand in the first half of 2027 than in the second half of 2026.
Old Dominion Freight Line ( NASDAQ: ODFL ) said its customers are seeking multiyear contracts as truck capacity tightens. It also noted that 3PLs are seeking longer-term capacity commitments.
Less-than-truckload stocks were up over 3% on average in early Monday trading. The S&P 500 was up 0.6%.
Why it matters? The ISM data provides key macroeconomic indicators that directly impact logistics, procurement and capacity planning. Changes in manufacturing activity serve as a leading indicator for LTL demand.

Warehouse leaders can’t predict every disruption , but they can prepare their facilities to adjust when plans fall apart. In this Q&A, Adam Brown , Senior Director for Market Intelligence at Dematic , discusses how simulation and flexible automation can help, and when it makes sense to rethink facility locations and inventory storage.
What’s Related
Supply Chain 24/7: You can’t plan for every disruption. So what makes a warehouse ready to handle something nobody saw coming?
Adam Brown: You can’t foresee every disruption, but you can prepare by identifying where your operation can adjust. If one piece of equipment goes down, can workflows adapt? If orders spike, do you know which part of the warehouse will reach its limit first? You may not know what the next disruption will be, but you can better understand how your operation is likely to respond.
That preparation goes beyond equipment. Employees need to know what to do when the normal process is interrupted, and backup plans need to be tested before anyone has to rely on them.
Software is a great solution to help teams spot trouble sooner. For example, Dematic Command Center brings together intelligence from across the system so teams can see where performance is slipping and what needs attention. That gives them time to act before a small issue becomes a bigger operational challenge.
RELATED STORIES: Before You Buy Warehouse Robots, Know What You’re Trying to Fix | Robots for the Rest of Us—Warehouse Automation Gets Easier
SC247: What’s a warning sign that a warehouse will struggle if demand suddenly jumps or the mix of orders changes?
Brown: A clear warning sign is when a relatively small change in demand creates a disproportionate increase in backlogs. If a modest jump in orders requires sustained overtime just to stay on schedule, the operation may not have room to absorb a larger disruption.
Order mix matters as much as total volume. A warehouse designed primarily to fulfill orders for retail stores may struggle when its order mix shifts toward e-commerce . Even if the overall number of units stays the same, the work required to fulfill those orders has changed.
Look at where work consistently piles up. That’s often where the right automation solution can make the biggest difference. Understanding those pressure points helps you choose the right approach, whether that means introducing more flexible automation or expanding an existing automated system. Planning for how that change affects the next step in the process helps the whole operation keep pace as demand grows.
SC247: For someone who hasn’t used a digital twin, how does it work, and what would you test first?
RELATED: Supply Chain 101: What Are Digital Twins and How Can They Benefit Your Company?
Brown: Think of a digital twin as a virtual version of your warehouse that uses intelligent operational data to help show how the facility behaves. It lets you test a change virtually before making it on the warehouse floor.
First, I’d make sure the model accurately reflects normal warehouse operations. Then I’d run a scenario the team recently experienced and compare the model’s results with what actually happened. Those checks help establish if the model is a reliable starting point for testing future disruptions.
Then I’d test a situation the team is concerned about. What happens if a key piece of equipment goes down during a busy shift? Can the backup process handle the work, or does it create a bottleneck somewhere else? That’s much better to find out in a model than with customer orders waiting to ship .
Adam Brown
SC247: Where can mobile robots and automated guided vehicles help an existing warehouse adjust, and where do they have limits?
Brown: Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and automated guided vehicles (AGVs) can automate repetitive movement between warehouse areas. Depending on the application, they can reduce employee travel or bring inventory directly to picking stations. They can also introduce automation in phases.
However, all technologies have limits. The vehicles need room to move, and their ability to navigate depends on the technology they use and conditions on the warehouse floor, including traffic and obstacles.
Adding more robots will make operations more efficient, but it won’t keep increasing output if other parts of the operation, such as picking, packing or shipping, can’t handle the additional volume. At some point, traffic can become a problem, or the receiving workstation may not be able to keep up. Automation aims to improve how goods move through the warehouse. The number of robots is only one part of that.
“Adding more robots will make operations more efficient, but it won’t keep increasing output if other parts of the operation, such as picking, packing or shipping, can’t handle the additional volume.”
SC247: How do you decide whether to change an existing warehouse, add another location, or rethink where you keep inventory?
Brown: Start by identifying what is limiting your business . A facility that lacks storage space presents a different problem than a distribution network that puts inventory too far from customers.
If the location still serves the business well, evaluate how much more capacity the existing facility can handle. Improving workflows or upgrading selected systems may create capacity without the cost of another building. High-density storage can also help when space is the main issue, provided it fits the building and the products being stored.
Sometimes the building is limiting business growth, or the business needs to serve customers in a different region. A new facility gives you more freedom to design around those needs, but it requires a larger investment and a longer timeline.
Putting inventory closer to customers can shorten delivery times. Existing brick-and-mortar stores are increasingly serving as mini-warehouses, supporting store replenishment and e-commerce fulfillment while keeping shipping costs competitive. However, they can also increase costs and require more stock across the network. You need to weigh that cost against the service improvement. The best choice should solve today’s problem and still make sense as the business grows.
SC247: How do you make the case for spending money on flexibility when the payoff might not come until something goes wrong?
“You don’t always need a major upgrade to be better prepared. Flexible automation also lets you start with one process and expand as your needs grow and your budget allows. Whether you’re fixing a recurring problem or introducing automation, a targeted investment can give the team time back now and take some pressure off when demand picks up.”
Brown: Investing in flexibility isn’t just about preparing for the future. You should determine how the investment can improve operations today. For example, reducing the time employees spend walking between tasks can improve daily productivity. It can also help the team manage a busier period with the people available. The same thinking applies to adding capacity in stages. A business can invest in what it needs now while leaving room to expand, rather than paying upfront for capacity it may not use for years.
Then put some numbers around the disruption you’re trying to prepare for. What would another week of overtime cost? What happens if orders can’t ship on time? How much does downtime impact your bottom line? Comparing those scenarios gives leaders a clearer sense of how much flexibility is worth paying for.
SC247: If a warehouse leader has a tight budget, what’s one practical change you’d suggest making now to prepare for the next disruption?
Brown: Start with a focused review of the part of the operation that most often slows everything else down. Look at recent stoppages and recurring jams to understand what is causing the lost time.
The answer may be a maintenance adjustment or a change in how work is released. If equipment failure is the concern, check that the right replacement part is available and employees know how to get the system running again.
You don’t always need a major upgrade to be better prepared. Flexible automation also lets you start with one process and expand as your needs grow and your budget allows. Whether you’re fixing a recurring problem or introducing automation, a targeted investment can give the team time back now and take some pressure off when demand picks up.
Adam Brown is Senior Director for Market Intelligence at Dematic

Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 2, 2026
Gold Fields (NYSE: GFI; JSE: GFI) has secured Quebec’s principal environmental approval for its Windfall gold project, clearing the way to restart underground development while it prepares a final investment decision.
The certificate, issued Oct. 30, completes the project’s provincial environmental and social impact review. Gold Fields will now pursue a mining lease and secondary permits, with an updated construction schedule, capital estimate and resource and reserve estimates expected by February alongside its provisional 2026 results, the company said Monday.
“Receiving the Certificate of Authorization for Windfall is a major milestone for Gold Fields and for one of Canada’s highest-grade development-stage gold projects,” CEO Mike Fraser said in a statement . “The Uukiimau Agreement and the Certificate of Authorization demonstrate how responsible mining can be advanced through respect, transparency and shared value creation.”
Windfall is expected to produce about 300,000 oz. of gold annually once ramped up, adding a Canadian operation to the South African producer’s portfolio. The approval removes a key development risk, although updated costs and the construction timetable remain important outstanding items, BMO mining analyst Raj Ray wrote in a note Monday.
Costs and timing
Development capital is expected towards the upper end of Gold Fields’ existing $1.7-billion to $1.9-billion guidance, equivalent to roughly C$2.4 billion to C$2.7 billion and expressed in 2025 U.S. dollars, the company said in August.
BMO models spending of $2.1 billion, about 11% above the upper end of company guidance, and first production in the second half of 2029, Ray wrote.
Underground activities were suspended after the project’s bulk-sample exploration permit expired at the end of August. Gold Fields had been awaiting the separate environmental authorization needed to advance construction.
Personnel and equipment will now be remobilized, with underground work resuming progressively. Early civil works and camp construction covered by existing board authorization will also begin shortly, the company said. The final investment decision remains subject to board approval.
Cree agreement
The environmental authorization follows the June signing of the Uukiimau impact and benefit agreement with the Cree First Nation of Waswanipi, the Cree Nation Government and the Grand Council of the Crees.
The agreement sets out commitments covering training, employment, business opportunities, environmental monitoring and financial participation over the project’s operating life.
Quebec’s Environmental and Social Impact Review Committee, known as COMEX, examined the development, including through public hearings in Lebel-sur-Quévillon and Waswanipi in spring 2026.
Windfall lies on Waswanipi’s traditional territory, about 115 km by road east of Lebel-sur-Quévillon. Windfall Mining Group, a wholly owned Gold Fields subsidiary, is developing the project.
Gold Fields secured full ownership in October 2024 through its C$2.16-billion takeover of Osisko . It had acquired an initial 50% interest in May 2023 for an upfront C$300 million.
Beyond Windfall, Gold Fields controls about 2,500 sq. km in the Urban-Barry and Quévillon areas, where regional exploration is targeting additional discoveries.

Parcel carriers will deliver about 2.4 billion packages during the current peak shipping season, up 4% from the same period last year, despite high inflation, according to an estimate from ShipMatrix.
The increase in parcel demand is aided by an extra shopping day this holiday season, said ShipMatrix, which helps shippers get more out of their FedEx ( NYSE: FDX ), UPS ( NYSE: UPS ) and regional carrier agreements.
The projected volume would be the highest level for the parcel industry since 2022, when the Covid-triggered spike in e-commerce reached its peak.
Consumers have remained resilient so far this year in the face of rising fuel costs and overall inflation, which have diminished discretionary income. But analysts worry that the cumulative impact of tightening household budgets eventually could trigger a pullback in retail sales.
Retailers have also experienced a 16% jump in parcel shipping rates compared to last year, largely driven by broad fuel surcharges, other new fees and general rate increases. Fuel surcharges currently represent about 30% of the transportation rate and most of the spike is the result of carriers adjusting the formula used to calculate the fee rather than the actual rise in fuel costs, according to the latest TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index . FedEx and UPS implemented 5.9% general rate increases this year and recently announced plans to repeat the price increase in 2027.
(Source: ShipMatrix)
Higher shipping charges have led some retailers to raise the minimum amount spent at checkout to qualify for free shipping.
UPS recently highlighted how its delivery network is better equipped this year to handle increased volumes thanks to new automation and RFID tracking technology. It said it will hire 100,000 temporary workers, down from 109,000 last year, to help keep packages flowing smoothly through distribution centers. Amazon, for its part, is hiring 300,000 seasonal workers, a 20% increase from last year. The U.S. Postal Service recently said it was ready for the upcoming peak season and plans to hire 10,000 seasonal workers.
The hiring differences reflect UPS’s decision to relinquish 50% of its Amazon ( NASDAQ: AMZN ) business because it wasn’t making money providing last-mile delivery service, UPS deploying more automated sorting machinery, and the broader shift of B2C parcel volume from legacy carriers to large retailers’ own delivery networks.
UPS has recently concentrated on high- margin , end-to-end logistics services for customers in many industry verticals, leading some to question whether it can maintain the parcel network for those deliveries without the density to offset the costs and generate sufficient margins.
In the first-half of 2026, total U.S. domestic parcel volumes increased for Amazon by 9.7% percent, thanks to the decoupling from UPS and its own delivery expansion into rural areas, according to the ShipMatrix analysis. FedEx volume increased 4.6%.
However, volume for UPS and the U.S. Postal Service decreased by 5.7% and 3.1%, respectively. The volume lost by UPS and USPS was more than the gain by Amazon and FedEx, with those additional 145 million packages being diverted by shippers to private networks of large retailers like Walmart, as well as alternate carriers like GoFo, Uni-Uni, SpeedX, Doordash, Jitsu, Veho, OnTrac, and Better Trucks, who have expanded their coverage area in the past two years, ShipMatrix said.
(Source: ShipMatrix)
FedEx and UPS continued to head in opposite directions in terms of volume during the third quarter.
FedEx’s average daily domestic package volume increased 2% during the third quarter, according to its earnings report. Drilling down further, during the past two quarters, average daily domestic volume for FedEx priority and deferred service increased 2.16% year over year, while average daily volume for more economical ground home and commercial delivery increased 3.5%.
UPS reported a 3.3% decline in average daily package volume. Year-to-date daily volume through September fell 4.9% compared to the same period last year.

After a year of controversial regulatory reversals, the FDA has accepted uniQure’s application for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec for priority review, with a May 1 action date. If approved, the therapy—also called AMT-130—would be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s disease.
At long last, the FDA has accepted uniQure’s embattled Huntington’s disease gene therapy for priority review, setting a May 1 decision date for the product, with a potential advisory committee meeting in the works.
Despite the investigational gene therapy showing a 75% slowing of disease after 36 months in a Phase 1/2 trial in September 2025, FDA officials at the time took issue with the design of the study and insisted that uniQure run a sham-controlled Phase 3 study before submitting an application for approval. After a reversal of guidance this spring, the biotech filed for approval of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec—also called AMT-130—on Sept. 2.
If approved, ifezuntirgene inilparvovec would be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s, a rare fatal, inherited neurodegenerative disorder that causes motor symptoms, behavioral abnormalities and cognitive decline.
Stifel analysts saw the biologics license application (BLA) acceptance as a positive sign for the therapy and biotech. “We think the BLA acceptance today, with priority review, represents an incrementally positive sign on the prospects of accelerated approval,” the group wrote in an investor note on Monday morning.

William Blair agreed with Stifel’s assessment. “We view this announcement as an incremental positive given that it supports the FDA’s willingness to review the application for accelerated approval,” the firm said in a Monday note to investors.
UniQure is anticipating that the FDA will call an advisory committee meeting for the application, since the agency stated that it is “tentatively planning to discuss this application” at an adcomm, the company said in a Monday morning press release .
UniQure has walked a rocky path to get to this moment. In November 2025—five weeks after revealing the three-year data that sparked excitement and optimism in the Huntington’s community—the FDA reversed previous guidance that such data would be sufficient to support an approval application. Instead, the agency said the data were not “adequate to provide the primary evidence in support of a BLA submission,” according to uniQure at the time.

A month after sparking optimism for patients with Huntington’s disease with highly positive data for AMT-130, uniQure revealed Monday that the FDA may be changing its tune on the evidence required for an approval application, a change of direction Stifel called “very challenging” for uniQure.

In the following months, then FDA Commissioner Marty Makary and Center for Biologics and Evaluation (CBER) director Vinay Prasad proceeded to make negative comments appearing to allude to the gene therapy. Both leaders have since left the agency.
Then in September this year, four-year data from the Phase 1/2 trial in were “weaker than expected,” Stifel wrote in Monday’s note, causing uniQure’s stock to drop by as much as 38%. The analysts noted that the company has traded down since.
In a statement on Monday, uniQure CEO Matt Kapusta called the BLA acceptance “an important milestone for the Huntington’s disease community, which has waited generations for a treatment that changes the course of this devastating disease.”
UniQure also provided an update Monday on the asset’s confirmatory trial, saying this “remains a key priority, with screening anticipated to begin by year end.” The company expects the study to be “well underway by the time of potential approval.”
The study will enroll around 200 patients randomized to receive ifezuntirgene inilparvovec or standard of care. The main goal will be total functional capacity—a primary scale used in Huntington’s to measure a patient’s ability to complete every-day tasks—over 36 months.

KYIV, Ukraine — A new pocket-sized receiver can co-opt video from Russian unmanned systems, allowing Ukrainian drone operators to intercept enemy live feeds in real time, the device’s makers said this month, while adding only a little extra weight to operators’ kits.
Kyiv communications-equipment maker CODE380 developed the D·Vision SDR , which uses a software-defined radio (SDR) to sweep frequencies from 500 megahertz to 8.7 gigahertz for drone signals and convert them into video, reducing common visibility problems and allowing easy software updates for new drone specs.
The D-Vision SDR scans its frequency range without “blind spots” and offers greater sensitivity than competing detectors, the developers told the Ukrainian tech outlet DOU on Oct. 17.
The receiver joins a growing set of cheap, passive Ukrainian drone sensors that listen for threats without emitting a signal that could give away a unit’s position, working alongside radar, acoustic sensors and interceptors rather than replacing them.
CODE380’s device can display analog video from drones up to 6 miles (10 kilometers) away on frequencies between 540 megahertz and 6 gigahertz, and from 2 to 3 miles (3.5 to 5 kilometers) away on higher frequencies, according to manufacturer figures reported by Militarnyi .
Analog drones broadcast their camera feed unencrypted, so a receiver tuned to the right frequency can show a unit where an attack is heading and what the pilot is aiming at before impact.
The receiver’s sweep covers the 4.1 to 4.5 gigahertz band where Russia’s Molniya strike drones began sending video in June, according to Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, presidential adviser and radio specialist.
“Most detectors don’t see these frequencies, or see them poorly,” he wrote in June. “I’m warning you so that trust in a detector doesn’t cost you your life.”
The D-Vision SDR is not the first Ukrainian receiver to tap drone video, but its receiver weighs less than half as much as its main domestic rivals at roughly 10 ounces (290 grams).
Babai’s roughly 2-pound (0.9-kilogram) Vydun 7.5 intercepts analog video up to 7.5 gigahertz, while Contra-drone’s 21-ounce (600-gram) SENSE-4 reaches 8.2 gigahertz and BlueBird Tech’s Chuyka 3.0 , which weighs up to 23 ounces (650 grams), can now be upgraded to 8.8 gigahertz, according to manufacturers.
Many receivers struggle to decode digital video, detect Mavic-compatible signals beyond a few miles, and pick up fiber-optic drones guided by cables.
Drone variants are already being designed with harder-to-hack video feeds, Beskrestnov said, pointing out Russia’s Molniyas as an example.
“We need to be ready for digital video to one day fully replace analog,” he wrote, warning that portable detectors and fixed analog receiving stations would then become ineffective.

Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 2, 2026
Canadian explorer Pecoy Copper (TSXV: PCU; US-OTC: PCUUF) agreed to raise $49.8 million (US$35.7 million) from Hudbay Minerals (TSX, NYSE: HBM) and another investor to fund drilling and technical studies at its copper-gold project in southern Peru. The stock rose.
Hudbay is to invest $30.1 million, while the unnamed investor committed $19.7 million, Pecoy said Monday . Each would hold just under 10% after closing, calculated on a partially diluted basis.
“We view the deal positively, as it validates Pecoy’s technical and geological quality, while strengthening the balance sheet at lower dilution than we had modelled,” Desjardins Capital Markets mining analyst Bryce Adams wrote Monday in a note.
The investment connects Pecoy with a producer that operates the Constancia copper mine in Peru. It also provides funding for drilling and studies needed to better define the deposit and assess how its metals could be recovered.
‘Strong endorsement’
Given Hudbay’s long history of operating in southern Peru, “we view their investment as providing a strong endorsement to the future potential of the Pecoy project,” National Bank Financial mining analyst Andrew Dusome said in a separate note.
Pecoy shares jumped 7.7% to $1.96 Monday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about $413 million. The stock has traded between 85¢ and $2.29 in the past year.
Vancouver-based Pecoy plans to issue about 24.7 million shares at $2.02 apiece, a 10% premium to its 10-day volume-weighted average price through Oct. 30. The subscription price is also 11% above Friday’s $1.82 close. Closing is expected around Thursday, subject to regulatory approvals, including TSX Venture Exchange acceptance.
Hudbay would receive rights to participate in future financings and top up its holdings to maintain ownership of up to 9.9%. Subject to ownership thresholds, it could nominate one director, or two if Pecoy’s board expands to at least 10 members. Both Hudbay and the unnamed investor had previously invested in Pecoy, CEO Vincent Metcalfe told The Northern Miner Monday via e-mail. Hudbay built its position through market acquisitions, while the second investor holds historical warrants, which haven’t been exercised yet, Metcalfe said.
Cash lift
The latest financing would lift Pecoy’s cash resources to roughly $70 million, enough for five to six quarters of spending, Adams said. His model had assumed a $50-million financing at $1.50 a share, requiring about 33.3 million new shares.
The financing “also improves funding visibility through the next phase of resource definition and technical work,” Scotiabank mining analyst Eric Winmill wrote Monday.
The explorer owns the Pecoy and Tororume projects in southern Peru’s Arequipa region. Pecoy lies about 275 km northwest of Arequipa, at an elevation of about 1,650 metres, near highway, power and port infrastructure.
Updated resource
An April 2025 resource for Pecoy estimate outlined 865 million inferred tonnes grading 0.34% copper, 0.012% molybdenum, 0.05 gram gold per tonne and 1.33 grams silver for contained metal of about 6.45 billion lb. copper. The estimate uses a 0.23% copper cut-off. These resources have not demonstrated economic viability.
Tororume, 8 km to the north, provides another exploration target. Previous owner Pembrook completed nine widely spaced drill holes between 2017 and 2023, intersecting copper and molybdenum mineralization. Pecoy says much of the system remains untested.
The new money will support resource expansion, geological work and metallurgical testing ahead of an updated Pecoy resource estimate. Adams expects that estimate early next year and a preliminary economic assessment later in 2027.

Interstate 94 ranked first in Trucker Path ’s 2026 assessment of major U.S. trucking corridors, narrowly beating I-90 in truck parking availability, truck stop ratings and diesel prices. I-80 placed third, giving northern routes all three top spots.
What’s Related
Trucker Path scored 19 corridors on a 100-point scale, with I-94 earning 94.20 points, followed by I-90 at 94.05 and I-80 at 93.75. The company gave parking availability more weight than the other measures, describing it as a consistently identified driver concern.
The results, distributed Oct. 28, ranked I-35 and I-15 fourth and fifth. The top 10 also included I-40, I-44, I-20, I-70, and I-45.
The ranking measures conditions at stops along the routes. Its three scoring categories exclude traffic congestion, pavement quality, and travel times, so read the results as a comparison of places to park, refuel , and take a break.

Parking leader finishes fifth overall
The highest-ranked corridor didn't lead every category. I-94 recorded parking availability of 83.9% and an average truck stop rating of 3.6, compared with 86.1% and 3.8 for second-place I-90.
I-15 had the highest parking availability among the top 10, at 87.3%, but finished fifth overall. Its listed average diesel price was also the highest in that group, at $6.81.
At the other end of the top 10, I-45 had the lowest listed diesel price, at $5.79, and the lowest parking availability, at 75.2%. The difference between its parking figure and I-15’s was 12.1 percentage points.

Nearly 80% of the waste haulers using TrashLab’s software now rely on its AI agent, Haul-E, to answer inbound calls and capture after-hours orders. On Thursday, TrashLab said it raised $12 million to build more agents like it.
The money funds agents for dispatch, billing, and collections that would move more of a hauler’s office work onto software.
“Since going live TrashLab has allowed us to grow our fleet 3x all while keeping the same lean backoffice team,” said Mike Smith, president of First State Waste, which runs roll-off, front-load, and portable toilet service.
What the platform replaces
TrashLab says its platform replaces the spreadsheets, paper routes, and older software haulers have long run on. It puts the call center and customer records, dispatch and routing, an in-cab driver app and truck cameras, billing and payments, and reporting in one system.
“Haulers have been forced to choose between antiquated tools and platforms that can’t handle more than one line of business,” said Neil Chaudhary, TrashLab’s co-founder and CEO.
At Uribe Refuse, truck cameras now feed billing.
“When the camera flags a can not out, a blocked dumpster, or an overflowed container, it moves from the field to a customer text to the invoice automatically,” said Brad Uribe, the company’s owner. He said his company is now “catching, billing, and resolving issues that used to fall through the cracks.”
Funding and growth
Ventana, an early-growth equity firm, led the Series A round. Existing investors Bienville Capital, Harlem Capital, and CreativeCo also participated.
Vinay Kumar, Ventana’s co-founder and partner, joins TrashLab’s board. Ershad Jamil, a former chief growth officer at ServiceTitan and BuildOps, joins as an independent director.
TrashLab said annual contract value has grown more than sevenfold since 2024 as customers add modules. It did not disclose revenue or the 2024 starting figure. The company said it serves hundreds of haulers across more than 40 states in the U.S. and Canada, and that haulers have managed more than 5 million tons of material on the platform since launch.
Waste hauling is a large and lucrative market. Waste Business Journal estimates U.S. waste and recycling revenue reached $104.63 billion in 2024, the first year it topped $100 billion.
Kumar called TrashLab “the fastest-growing platform we’ve seen in an industry that has been underserved by software for decades.”
Rollout timeline
TrashLab’s dispatch, billing, and collections agents are still being built, with rollout planned through 2027.
TrashLab was founded in 2022 by Chaudhary, a former BCG and EY-Parthenon consultant, and John Tan, its chief technology officer and a former senior engineer at Stripe and Google. The company plans to expand its engineering and customer success teams in the coming months.
“Our customers see a return from fuel savings, leaner back offices, and faster collections within weeks of going live,” Chaudhary said. “Haul-E, our AI agent, is already answering calls and taking orders for most of them — and it’s the first of many agents we’re building into the platform.”
Why it matters: TrashLab is selling haulers on adding trucks without adding office staff, as First State Waste says it did. What could slow it: its dispatch, billing, and collections agents roll out through 2027.

Early reports from Amazon, Tractor Supply and Carter’s point to an uneven environment heading into the holiday season, with shipping inflation alongside isolated delays in getting merchandise into inventory.
A focus on efficiency pointed up how effectively retailers can offset external cost pressures by improving the movement and placement of goods. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) reported benefits from its fulfillment network, while Tractor Supply (NASDAQ: TSCO ) cited transportation costs as a drag on margins. Carter’s (NYSE: CRI ), meanwhile, reported inbound shipping disruptions that left inventory below plan.
Amazon said on its earnings call that its fulfillment operations faced higher fuel costs and line-haul rates on long distance trucking between facilities. Better inventory placement, shorter shipping distances and package consolidation nevertheless helped lower its cost to serve customers.
Shipping costs rose 11% from a year earlier, compared with a 12% increase in units. Excluding fuel and line-haul inflation, shipping expenses increased 8%, indicating that operational improvements helped the company handle additional volume without a proportionate increase in shipping costs.
Tractor Supply’s third-quarter results showed a more direct effect from rising logistics expenses. The company attributed gross- margin pressure primarily to higher transportation and fuel costs, alongside investments in pricing.
Gross margin declined to 36.4% from 37.4% a year earlier, even as sales increased 5.1%. Retailers are facing added pressures from rising distribution expenses while they continue investing in competitive prices.
Carter’s highlighted a challenge in the timing of inventory arrivals. Management said on its third-quarter call that port congestion and container availability issues had left inventory somewhat below plan.
Inventory totaled $587 million, down 11% from a year earlier. The company said the disruptions had not materially affected its business to date.

A view of the 1.2-km-long Connection drift that broke through in March 2025. Credit: West Red Lake Gold Mines
Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 2, 2026
West Red Lake Gold Mines (TSXV: WRLG; US-OTC: WRLGF) has agreed terms for a loan of up to $95 million (C$132.8 million) to lower borrowing costs and support its Ontario operations after cutting this year’s gold production target by about a quarter.
The binding term sheet with Gunvor USA, a subsidiary of Centalion Group, provides for an initial loan of up to $65 million and a further loan of up to $30 million subject to additional conditions, the company said Monday. Funding requires due diligence, definitive agreements and approvals. The money would refinance Nebari debt and support Madsen, about 260 km east-northeast of Winnipeg, and potential development at Rowan.
“Over the course of the year, we have built a strong business relationship with Centalion, culminating in a financing arrangement that would provide West Red Lake Gold with increased liquidity, a more competitive cost of capital and significantly improved repayment terms,” CEO Shane Williams said in the release. “This represents an important step in strengthening our financial position.”
Cheaper debt would ease financing costs while the company works to establish reliable output. Red Cloud Securities analyst Ian Parkinson viewed last week’s operating update as slightly negative in an Oct. 28 note, citing reliance on lower-grade remnant areas. Parkinson identified the forthcoming Madsen–Rowan prefeasibility study as the key catalyst for a shift toward higher-grade ore from previously unmined ground.
The financing proposal follows a 26% reduction in the midpoint of Madsen’s annual production guidance last week. Labour shortages and difficult mining in previously worked areas have slowed an operation that declared commercial production in January. Previous operator Pure Gold Mining shut Madsen and entered creditor protection in October 2022 after failing to generate consistent positive site-level cash flow. West Red Lake acquired the mine in June 2023.
Shares gained 7.7% to C56¢ by mid-Monday in Toronto, valuing the company at C$232.1 million. They’ve traded between C52¢ and C$1.49 over the past year.
Cheaper borrowing
The proposed loan would carry interest at one-month secured overnight financing rate, or SOFR, plus 5.5%. It would mature five years after the initial draw, with no scheduled principal repayments on the first tranche for nine months.
That compares with the existing Nebari loan, originally capped at $35 million, which charges three-month SOFR plus 8%. Its benchmark-rate floor of 4% means a minimum annual interest rate of 12%. The original maturity was 42 months after the first draw on Dec. 31, 2024. The proposed interest margin is 2.5 percentage points lower, although the loans use different benchmark tenors.
Gunvor would receive senior security over Madsen and Rowan and purchase all gold doré produced by the operation.
At June 30, West Red Lake carried C$43.7 million under the Nebari loan and held C$31.2 million in cash, according to its interim financial statements. Part of the proceeds would repay Nebari rather than provide new working capital.
Operating strain
Madsen produced 7,859 oz. in the third quarter, down 8.4% from the previous three months, bringing nine-month output to 22,102 ounces. The company now expects 27,000 to 32,000 oz. this year, down from 35,000 to 45,000 ounces.
West Red Lake has added specialized contractors and commissioned a secondary crusher to improve material handling. It is developing additional mining fronts, including previously unmined areas deeper in the deposit.
The integrated study would assess a combined production plan using Madsen’s mill to process ore from Rowan as an underground satellite operation. The company expects to release the study in the coming weeks, it said Oct. 27.
